narrative.overview:
The site is the exercise book it prints. The interface is the cover — a light board stock (#f5f5f0), a shade heavier than the sheet it holds, the way a school notebook's cover is a field and not a white page. Squared paper (#ffffff) appears only where real paper appears: the printable worksheet, the static prose plate, the settings panel and the answer key. Everything else stands on the board.

The Governing Rule: cover carries the interface; paper is reserved for where real paper is. There is no dark field to do the separating, so the split is carried by three things together, and all three are load-bearing: TONE (the board is a shade darker than the sheet, and the two must never converge — they ship only 1.15:1 apart, so this carrier is the weakest of the three), EDGE (a 1px ink hairline drawn around every paper plate), and LIFT (a tight, short-throw shadow under the sheet). Remove any one and the page collapses into a single cream expanse.

Mode is Operate: a hurried adult picks a worksheet, adjusts it, and prints. Density is moderate and legibility outranks it — the screen is read over a shoulder by a six-year-old. The world refuses the pastel kids-edu register: no rounded illustration icons in tinted squares, no chimes, no stars, no gradient candy. It also refuses a dark ground: this is stationery, and stationery is light.
keyCharacteristics: One light board field, one warm mark colour, one paper stock, held apart by tone + edge + lift.
Paper surfaces sit on the board as square-cut plates with a hairline keyline plus a tight shadow — stapled stock, not floating glass.
Nine subject inks, carried as a 4–5px edge tab, as a card head band, and as the tint on the dense-context icons — never as text.
Type is Archivo for cover/display, Inter for UI and prose, JetBrains Mono for every figure.
The notebook square (--sq: 26px) is the shared module between the sheet and the chrome that configures it.
Motion is one authored moment: the set stamp coming down.

rules.name: The Cover/Paper Rule
rules.body: No surface is both, and the two never converge in tone. Cover and paper are only 1.15:1 apart; a new paper plate must therefore state its own color: var(--color-text) and carry box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--edge) plus --shadow-sm/--shadow-md. A paper surface without its edge and lift is invisible.

rules.name: The One Warm Mark Rule
rules.body: Marking red is the product's single warm colour and it belongs to the act of making paper. Do not use it for chips, badges, headings, dividers, or decoration.

rules.name: The Grayscale Rule
rules.body: On paper, colour is never the sole carrier of meaning. Every printed distinction survives a grayscale inkjet: states are named in words, and the sheet's marks are ink-black, not tinted.

rules.name: The Ink Discipline Rule
rules.body: No decorative grey on paper. Print overrides push every screen grey to a real ink value — field labels #333, rules #333, problem numbers #555, the stamp #111 — so every printed mark carries information.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader compares or aligns is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums in JetBrains Mono: problem values, the set stamp, problem counters, answer-key numbers and values. Digits never render through toLocaleString().

rules.name: The Named Face Rule
rules.body: Three loaded families and no fourth. No system display face, and no icon font — every icon is inline stroked SVG.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element declares min-height: 44px — nav links, footer links, brand label, back button, language button and menu items, catalog rows and chips, buttons, checkbox rows, sliders, fold summaries.

rules.name: The Keyline-First Rule
rules.body: Separation on the board is a 1px ink ring at low alpha, not a border and not a heavier shadow. A paper plate that drops its keyline has broken the governing rule, not just lost a detail.

rules.name: The Flat Cover Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the board is elevated except paper. Board-side controls (nav links, back button, sidebar rows, resume card, empty state) use cover-wash / cover-wash-strong tonal washes instead of shadow.

rules.name: The Stroked-Mark Rule
rules.body: Every mark in the interface is drawn: sheet miniatures are hand-authored SVG at one stroke weight and one 8px grid pitch (SheetThumb.jsx); interface icons are inline stroked SVG (Tabler, stroke 1.7–2.0, 19–26px), tinted with the subject ink. No icon font, no emoji, no raster glyph, no illustration-in-a-tinted-square.

rules.name: The Two-Cue Rule
rules.body: In a dense list the icon is the faster cue and the colour is the second one. Colour alone carries nothing for a viewer who cannot separate the hues, so a subject ink never travels without either its icon or its label. The full catalog keeps the drawn sheet miniatures instead: at card size the real sheet is more informative than any icon.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Guarantee
rules.body: A global prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block clamps every animation and transition to 0.01ms with a single iteration, and the stamp explicitly sets animation: none. Paper never animates: the stamp is also disabled in @media print.

rules.name: The Print Shorthand Rule
rules.body: Inside @media print, never use the `background` shorthand on a surface another rule paints a background-image onto. The shorthand also resets background-size/origin/position/repeat, and at equal specificity it wins those longhands even when a later rule wins the image — which is how every notebook worksheet came to print with `background-size: auto` and no ruling at all. Restate the geometry longhands next to the print background-image.

rules.name: The Ruled-To-The-Edge Rule
rules.body: A printed notebook sheet is ruled to the bottom margin, not to the last problem. The sheet carries min-height: calc(var(--nb-page-sq) * var(--nb-sq)); --nb-page-sq is PAGE_SQUARES from useNotebookGrid, the page’s own square budget, so the ruling fills the page and can never push a second one.

rules.name: The Preview-On-Its-Ruling Rule
rules.body: A catalog preview draws squared paper, so every mark in it is placed in the ruling’s coordinates — never in free pixels. Use cx/cy/ln/span in SheetThumb: a digit is centred in a cell at the sheet’s own 0.77 digit-to-square ratio, a rule falls on a grid line, a blank is ink inside a cell. A mark at an arbitrary offset breaks the only claim the preview makes.

rules.name: The Masthead Rule
rules.body: The wordmark is set on the cover stock, never on a paper plate. Paper is reserved for where real paper is, and a wordmark is not a sheet — giving it a keyline, a lift and a hover rise put it beside the language button and made the pair read as two buttons. Identity is carried by the cover face and the drawn ruler mark. It is still a link home, so it owes an affordance: a ruled underline on the wordmark only, in --cover-line-strong, never a colour shift or a lift.

rules.name: The Three-Step Radius Rule
rules.body: Every corner in the app is --radius-sm (6px), --radius (8px) or --radius-lg (12px). Plates take the large step, controls the default, small marks the small one. A 2-3px scale was tried and read as too sharp for a product a six-year-old sits in front of. A literal px radius in a component file is drift in either direction.

dos: Do put paper only where a sheet, a leaf, or a sheet's control panel is; everything else stands on the board.
Do give every new paper surface all three separators: its own color: var(--color-text), a 1px var(--edge) keyline, and --shadow-sm/--shadow-md. On a light board, one of the three is not enough.
Do keep cover and paper apart in tone. They ship 1.15:1 apart — the whole remaining margin; any change that closes that gap deletes the system.
Do build board-side hover and raised states from cover-wash / cover-wash-strong, tinted from the ground's own ink.
Do spend marking red only on the Print action, the focus ring, prose links (mark-deep) and the set stamp.
Do pair every subject ink with an icon or a text label — colour is the second cue, never the only one.
Do set every figure in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums.
Do give every interactive element min-height: 44px.
Do convert every screen grey to a real ink value inside @media print.
Do budget the tallest translation when computing rows per printed page.
donts: Don't introduce a dark ground. The world is stationery and stationery is light; the ink-navy field was tried and rejected outright.
Don't ship a paper plate without its keyline. Without the edge it is a cream shape on a cream field.
Don't use white-tinted washes on the board. White on light board is invisible; washes are ink-tinted.
Don't use a subject ink as text, as a fill, or as the only signal of state.
Don't use marking red for badges, headings, dividers or decoration.
Don't treat control-navy as a ground. It is a control accent (toggle fill, accent-color, focus border) and nothing larger.
Don't put on-cover-muted text on cover-deep — it measures 4.40:1 there.
Don't put decorative grey on paper: every printed mark carries information and must survive grayscale on a cheap inkjet.
Don't use an icon font, emoji, or a raster glyph. Interface icons are inline stroked SVG at 1.7–2.0 stroke; sheet miniatures are drawn SVG at one weight and one grid pitch.
Don't put an icon in the full catalog in place of the sheet miniature — at card size the real sheet is the argument.
Don't add a second authored animation. The set stamp is the product's one moment; feedback that rewards a tap is the thing this product argues against.
Don't add uppercase editorial kickers or eyebrows above titles. The 11px uppercase style belongs to ruled document field captions (NAME / DATE / SET NO.) only.
Don't clip focus rings: no overflow: hidden on control containers.
Don't force a paper size in @page. Orientation only; lay out to the Letter/A4 intersection.

Don't rule a coloured band across the head of a card. The subject colour belongs in the shadow the sheet casts (color-mix on --card-color, declared after a neutral shadow), not in a strip between the card edge and its content.
Don't leave a cool hue on the paper. The ruling was slate-400 long after the palette went warm and read lavender on cream; screen and print ruling are neutral ink at the same blended lightness.
Don't put the brand on a paper plate, or give it a hover lift. In the header the only boxed element is the language switcher, because it is the only control.

Don't paint a coloured board behind the interface. An ink-navy field and a cream one were both built and both rejected — the navy for being dark, the cream for reading as aged paper. Chrome is white; the page tint is #f5f5f0 and nothing else.
contrast: faded board text on board 4.89:1 (4.40:1 on cover-deep — do not use it there)
focus ring on board 3.56:1 / on paper 4.47:1
cover vs paper 1.15:1 — tone alone is nowhere near the separator; edge and lift are
deviations: The direction contract's FIRST VIEWPORT called for the catalog as cover label-strips; the build shipped a paper card grid (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(268px, 1fr)), 940px). The label-strip form survives only in the compact sidebar/chip mode.
Equation Explorer's controls sit outside the shared settings panel (.eq-controls, its own layout), breaking the FIXED PANEL discipline that holds for the other eight worksheets.
notCanonized: The mobile hero at 14px (.catalog-hero, <=768px), a step below body size and far under the desktop 30px. Drift, not a ramp step; do not derive a mobile display size from it.

Resolved: ink-compare was #c07f1e at 2.58:1 on the board, under the 3:1 non-text floor. It is now #9a6212 (3.94:1 board, 4.95:1 paper); all nine subject inks clear 3:1 on both grounds and a new one must too.
The navy-tinted --shadow-sm / --shadow-md values (rgba(16,47,77,...)), left over from the dark-ground build. The ink tint (rgba(26,31,36,...)) used by --edge and the card-hover shadow is the rule.
The .worksheet keyline written as a literal rgba(16,47,77,0.16) rather than var(--edge), and the faint navy gradient wash on .catalog-card-sheet. Pre-relight residue, not tokens to copy.
